reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one change: OpenCode 2 does not load OpenCode 1 plugins, so on OpenCode 2 Notifai's generated OpenCode plugin never runs. `notifai doctor` now reads `opencode --version` when OpenCode is wired and reports a new readiness state, hooks-opencode-plugin ("OpenCode plugin loadability"): ready on OpenCode 1 or an unreadable version, a harness-scoped gap with a user-elsewhere remedy on OpenCode 2 or later, so it never blocks init or another harness's session. `notifai hooks install --harness opencode` still writes the plugin and adds a stderr warning on OpenCode 2. The OpenCode harness reference and the README support row now say the integration covers OpenCode 1 and that OpenCode 2 does not load the plugin yet. OpenCode 1 behavior, the generated plugin, hook definitions, commands and flags are unchanged. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one runtime change: Grok's imported copies of Notifai's Claude Code and Cursor hooks (`hook ... --harness claude-code` or `--harness cursor`, run by Grok's hook runner, which sets GROK_HOOK_EVENT) now end silently with exit 0 in the native launcher on macOS and Linux, before the session child, the hub or the runtime, and at the runtime entry elsewhere; the in-process guard already ignored them. Grok runs async handlers in line, so the Claude Code attend copy had held each Grok prompt and turn end for about 20 seconds. Grok's own Notifai hooks, real Claude Code and Cursor hooks, and Grok's tool shells (which carry no GROK_HOOK_EVENT) are unchanged. The Grok harness reference already says native Notifai hooks do not need imported Claude or Cursor copies, which still holds, and no agent action changes. No hook definition, command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shared skill, harness setup, readiness and domain terms. A root agent that uses Codex's synchronous request_user_input or Grok's question card in a signed-in, enabled Project with question notifications on now gets PostToolUse context saying the question never reached the User's devices and to ask with notifai ask; both harnesses hand hook context to the model only with the tool result, so no new handler or /hooks approval is added and the form itself is never denied. init --json returns the prepared machine-approval message in technical.pairing.message, and harness-setup.md sends it as written instead of fetching a template from the website. update --resume, doctor's npm repair status, the installer's legacy-npm collision and install --recover-integration name references/npm-migration.md or references/hermes-publication-recovery.md where each applies. send writes a non-blocking stderr note for a Summary of 200 or more characters or a Body over 1,500. Claude Code and Codex run Stop detached and discard its block decision, so their next prompt now also carries an owed answer acknowledgement, as it already did for Session Messages. Earlier review retained: Session start, the Cursor rule, the skill description and its "Decide whether to notify" section now say that an Agent Session another agent started with a task brief reports Agent Events to that agent and sends no Notification Requests unless the brief delegates them; a session the User started still owns them. Reviewed on top of Windows form linking. Merged with main after the Claude Code picker change (notes-only picker answers recorded as the terminal answer; report-only Remote Control expiry line), which was reviewed with no guidance impact; the two changes touch separate surfaces.
